title: Kernel hedging with online causality tests for mixed prefill/decode workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We observe intermittent latency regressions and cost spikes in mixed workloads (short-chat decode bursts interleaved with long-prefill requests) that are not captured by our existing seqlen-bucketed autotuners. Root cause analysis shows microarchitectural interactions (occupancy, kernel-launch contention) and phase-dependent attention path performance as triggers. Goal: introduce a lightweight hedging layer that runs short, targeted probes and applies online causality tests to decide when to switch kernel candidates or enable a safe fallback. The system should be seqlen- and arch-aware, minimally add CPU/GPU overhead, and integrate with prefill/decode scheduling to avoid oscillations. Success metrics: 95th percentile latency reduction in mixed-burst traces (target: 15% improvement vs baseline), reduced regression incidence during rollouts, and <2% additional compute overhead from probing. Constraints: can't rely on long offline profiling; must operate under production tail loads and co-exist with batching/caching policies.
acceptance_criteria: Hedging layer can detect a causal shift in kernel performance and switch to a fallback within 2s for sustained regressions
Integrated probes add <2% GPU time over a 24h traffic sample
No more than 1% false-positive kernel switches on synthetic stable workloads
End-to-end tests covering prefill->decode handoffs verify no token loss or KV cache corruption after kernel switch
Documentation and an ops runbook exist for enabling/disabling hedging per-customer or per-route
design_notes: Core idea: maintain a tiny runtime hedger that watches a small set of signals (per-kernel p95 latency, per-kernel occupancy estimate, queue length, and model-specific attention path counters). Periodically (or on trigger events) emit micro-probes: 1-2 single-request microbenchmarks that exercise a kernel on a short synthetic prefill or decode path. Apply an online causality test (Granger-style lightweight test adapted to streaming) across the signal stream to estimate whether observed latency changes are likely attributable to a kernel/arch interaction vs external noise (batching, network). If causality passes threshold, switch to a precomputed fallback kernel (quantized/alternative attention implementation) with a guarded canary: route 10% of traffic for 30s then escalate. Integration: link hedger with prefill scheduler so probes avoid competing during heavy prefill windows; annotate rollout policies to disable hedging on strict throughput SLAs. Implementation will be a runtime shim + small state store in-memory per-executor with eviction and TTL for probes. Use existing kernel metadata catalog (signature, compatible seq-len ranges, estimated cost) to select hedging candidates.
experiments_plan: Phase A (bench-only): run microbenchmarks across representative archs (A100, H100, L4) and model families (GPT-like, encoder-decoder) to calibrate causality thresholds. Phase B (shadow): enable hedger in shadow on 3 production routes for 48h, collect probe success/failure, false positives. Phase C (canary): enable on 10% traffic for a single region with automatic rollback if 95th latency regresses. Observability: add per-probe event logging (probe_id, kernel_from, kernel_to, seq_len_bucket, decision_score), and a dashboard for probe health and switch frequency.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime shim behind feature flag. 2) Deploy to staging with synthetic workload for prefill/decode mixes. 3) Shadow mode to collect data (2-3 days). 4) Canary 10% traffic for region us-west with automatic rollback. 5) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% if metrics stable for 72h. Ops controls: global kill-switch, per-customer disable, and a conservative mode that only monitors without switching.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: probe-induced contention during heavy burst windows. Mitigation: integrate with prefill scheduler and backoff probes when observed queue depth > threshold.
Risk: oscillation between kernels causing instability. Mitigation: hysteresis windows, minimum dwell time after switch (e.g., 60s), and exponential backoff for repeated switches.

Risk: inaccurate causality detection under highly non-stationary traffic. Mitigation: require corroborating signals (latency + occupancy + queue length) before switch; fall back to conservative thresholds.
Risk: increased tail latency for sensitive customers. Mitigation: per-customer opt-out and safe-mode where hedger only recommends but does not act.
Risk: extra telemetry volume. Mitigation: sample probe telemetry and compress event payloads; keep TTL for probe logs to 7 days by default.
